beats.say: Hello! Now let us look at a call in the operator's name: an offer to renew your SIM for free.
The screen can show the operator's name and a familiar number. Both can be faked.
Never tell a code you receive to a caller, even one who says they are the operator, bank or police.
If your operator offers an account PIN, set one. It makes a SIM swap harder.

question.prompt: A caller from the operator says: we are renewing your SIM, read me the code. What do you do?

options.label: I hang up and call the operator's official number myself
options.feedback: Correct. When you call the official number yourself, you know who you are talking to.

options.label: The number is the operator's, so I read the code
options.feedback: The number on the screen can be faked. This code moves your number onto someone else's card.

options.label: I ask for the caller's name and staff number
options.feedback: A criminal can make up a name and a number. The only real check is a call you make yourself.

scenes.explain: A call that asks for a code is the most dangerous call. Hang up and call the operator yourself.

scenes.title: Call from SahilTel
scenes.intro: Your phone is ringing. Read what the caller says and choose your answer.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What matters is that you give no code.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. If you are worried, call the operator yourself.

steps.say: Hello, this is Gunel from SahilTel. Old SIM cards, excuse me, are being switched off this month, so we are renewing yours for free.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> this is Gunel from SahilTel. Old SIM cards <cough> excuse me, are being switched off this month, so we are renewing yours for free.

actions.label: All right, what should I do?
actions.feedback: You have lost nothing yet, but the talk is heading for a code. Be careful.

actions.label: I will call the operator's official number myself
actions.feedback: Correct. If a renewal is real, the official line will confirm it.

actions.label: End call
actions.feedback: Good decision. Check any offer you did not expect on the official line.

steps.say: You just got a six digit code on your phone. Read it to me so the new card can be activated.
steps.spoken: You just got a six digit code on your phone. <breath> Read it to me so the new card can be activated.

actions.label: I read the code
actions.feedback: With this code your number moves to the criminal's card. From now on bank codes go to them.

actions.label: I do not tell the code to anyone
actions.feedback: Correct. The code is for you alone, whoever asks for it.

actions.label: End call
actions.feedback: Well done. Ending a call that asks for a code is the best answer.

steps.say: If you do not tell me the code, your number will be switched off tonight. This is the standard procedure, we are short on time.
steps.spoken: If you do not tell me the code, <breath> your number will be switched off tonight. This is, uh, the standard procedure, we are short on time.

actions.label: Fine, I will tell you the code
actions.feedback: The threat is there to rush you. If you give the code, your number goes to the criminal tonight.

actions.label: If needed, I will come to your office myself
actions.feedback: Good answer. If a new SIM is ever needed, you can change it yourself at the operator's office.

actions.label: End call
actions.feedback: Right. When the pressure grows, end the conversation.

steps.label: The call has ended. What do you do now?

actions.label: Call the operator's official number
actions.feedback: Correct. Report the call and ask whether you can set an account PIN.

actions.label: Call back the number that called
actions.feedback: That number may lead to the criminal. Take the number from the operator's official website.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The criminal will try again another way. Telling the operator protects your number.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation with the right step.

pairs.left: A caller asks for a code
pairs.right: Do not say it, end the call

pairs.left: Your phone suddenly shows No service
pairs.right: Call the operator from another phone

pairs.left: Your operator offers an account PIN
pairs.right: Set it and tell no one

pairs.left: A key account is protected only by SMS codes
pairs.right: Switch to an authenticator app or a passkey

scenes.explain: Never tell a code to anyone, act fast when your number dies, and do not let key accounts depend on SMS alone.

question.prompt: When is it fine to tell someone a code sent to your phone?

options.label: Never: I only type it into a site or app I opened myself
options.feedback: Correct. A code is like your signature and must stay in your hands only.

options.label: If the caller knows my name and personal ID number
options.feedback: Those details may have leaked. Anyone who knows you and still asks for the code is a fraudster.

options.label: If a relative asks for it in a message
options.feedback: Your relative's account may be taken over too. Call them yourself with a normal phone call.

scenes.explain: Banks and government bodies do not ask for SMS codes. Whoever asks for the code, end the conversation.

points: Never tell anyone a code you receive, whoever is calling
End a suspicious call and call the operator's official number yourself
If your operator offers an account PIN, set one
